name: Married Wing Mickey Finn
imitates: The quill-wing version of the Mickey Finn bucktail, a classic brook trout streamer; the married yellow-red-yellow wing gives it the traditional look.
recipe: Red goose or swan quill segments, left and right
Yellow hackle, wound and bound down as a beard
Left and right quill slips, yellow-red-yellow married

steps.text: Start the thread behind the eye, wrap to the bend and tie in a tail of red quill slips (three fibers wide from a right and a left feather), tips up and together, about a shank long.
Tie in small oval tinsel and a pointed length of medium flat tinsel on the far side of the hook, and bind them down along the shank.
Wrap the flat tinsel forward to form the body and tie it off without trimming it yet.
Wrap the oval tinsel forward in about five ribs, tie off and trim both tinsels.
Tie in a yellow hackle by the tip so the fibers reach the hook point when wound.
Wind the hackle and bind it down into a beard under the hook, rather than tying in a bunch of fibers.
Tie in the married wings low and level, tips up and together, reaching the end of the tail. Trim the butts and form a black thread head, then whip finish.
Finish the head with penetrating head cement followed by a lacquer coat. The finished fly is shown.

source.name: Fly Fishers International (Fly of the Month, Dec 2025)
source.author: Eric Austin
